metadata.title: qwen image layered - layered RGBA image decomposition and editing model
metadata.description: qwen image layered is an open-source diffusion model that decomposes a single RGB image into editable RGBA layers for precise image editing and compositing.
metadata.keywords: qwen image layered, Qwen-Image-Layered, RGBA layers, layer decomposition, image editing, diffusion model

hero.description: qwen image layered is an open-source diffusion model that decomposes a single RGB image into editable RGBA layers for precise image editing and compositing.

paragraphs: Qwen-Image-Layered is a newly released AI model from the Qwen team at Alibaba. It decomposes a single RGB image into multiple semantically disentangled RGBA layers, enabling inherent editability without extra masking or manual cutouts.

Each layer isolates an element like an object, background, or text, so it can be resized, repositioned, recolored, removed, or replaced without affecting other layers. The model supports variable numbers of layers (typically 3-10, with common options like 3 or 8) and even recursive decomposition so one layer can be split into sub-layers for finer control.

items.label: Input
items.description: Provide an image and optionally a prompt to guide the decomposition, such as the layer count or structure.

items.label: Output
items.description: A set of RGBA layers (RGB plus alpha transparency) that can be composited back into the original image.

items.label: Editing
items.description: High-fidelity edits like recoloring an object, swapping a subject, revising text, or moving elements while preserving consistency.

how_it_works.note: The system is an end-to-end diffusion model trained for layered representations, moving beyond flat pixels to a structured, editable format.

items.title: Inherent editability
items.description: Physically isolated layers enable clean edits without artifacts or extra masking tools.

items.title: Flexible structure
items.description: Prompt-controlled layer layouts support design, content creation, and AI-assisted editing.

items.title: Open-source
items.description: Fully available for free use, including commercial applications.

items.title: Applications
items.description: Ideal for graphic design, content generation, and advanced image manipulation in tools like ComfyUI.

items.title: Hugging Face
items.description: Model weights and a demo space for quick testing.

items.title: arXiv paper
items.description: Qwen-Image-Layered: Towards Inherent Editability via Layer Decomposition.

resources.note: For quick experiments, start with the Hugging Face demo embedded above.

problem.description: Recent visual generative models struggle with consistency during image editing because raster images entangle all visual content into a single canvas, leading to semantic drift and geometric misalignment in editing methods. Qwen-Image-Layered addresses this by decomposing images into semantically disentangled RGBA layers, allowing independent manipulation of each layer without affecting others.

paragraphs: Qwen-Image-Layered is an end-to-end diffusion model that takes a single RGB image I in R^(H x W x 3) and decomposes it into N RGBA layers L in R^(N x H x W x 4). Layers are reconstructed via sequential alpha blending:

The model supports variable-length decomposition (up to 20 layers) through an RGBA-VAE for shared latent spaces, a VLD-MMDiT architecture for layer prediction, and a multi-stage training strategy. A custom data pipeline processes Photoshop documents (PSD) to create multilayer training data.

cards.title: RGBA-VAE
cards.description: This variational autoencoder handles both RGB and RGBA inputs in a unified latent space to minimize distribution gaps. The encoder and decoder extend from 3 to 4 channels with alpha initialized to preserve RGB reconstruction. Training uses reconstruction, perceptual, and regularization losses, and layers are encoded independently without cross-layer interactions.

cards.title: VLD-MMDiT
cards.description: The Variable Layers Decomposition MMDiT uses flow matching with rectified flow. It encodes input RGB latents and predicts target layer latents, incorporates text prompts via Qwen2.5-VL, and applies Layer3D RoPE for variable-length layers. Visual sequences and text are concatenated for intra- and inter-layer attention.

items: Unified latent space via RGBA-VAE, unlike prior separate VAEs that introduce gaps.
Layer-wise attention in VLD-MMDiT with Layer3D RoPE for variable-length support and multi-task compatibility.
Multi-stage training to progressively adapt pretrained models and avoid direct finetuning issues.
PSD-based data pipeline using psd-tools to extract layers, filter anomalies, merge non-overlapping elements, and generate captions with Qwen2.5-VL.

training.description: Training uses a multi-stage approach on custom multilayer datasets derived from PSD files and internal data, totaling 1.3M steps with Adam at a 1e-5 learning rate. Stages include text-to-RGB/RGBA, text-to-multi-RGBA, and image-to-multi-RGBA for decomposition. The objective is flow matching loss on predicted velocity. Built on Qwen-Image, supporting up to 20 layers.

items: Decomposition evaluated on the Crello dataset for image-to-multi-RGBA (I2L), including open-domain and text-heavy images.
Editing demonstrates recoloring, repositioning, resizing, removal, and revision.
Synthesis compares text-to-multi-RGBA (T2L) against raster generation followed by decomposition.
Reconstruction tested on the AIM-500 dataset.
Decomposition on Crello uses RGB L1 distance (weighted by ground-truth alpha, lower is better) and Alpha soft IoU (higher is better) with order-aware DTW alignment and layer merging.
Reconstruction on AIM-500 uses PSNR, SSIM, rFID, and LPIPS on blended RGBA images over backgrounds.

paragraphs: Quantitative results show Qwen-Image-Layered-I2L reaching RGB L1 = 0.0363 and Alpha soft IoU = 0.9160 on Crello (merge = 5), outperforming LayerD and VLM+Hi-SAM. Ablations without Layer3D RoPE, RGBA-VAE, or multi-stage training drop sharply.

RGBA-VAE reconstruction scores include PSNR 38.8252, SSIM 0.9802, rFID 5.3132, and LPIPS 0.0123, outperforming LayerDiffuse and AlphaVAE. Qualitatively, the model produces clean layer decomposition without artifacts and consistent edits.

Community reactions on X highlight its potential for ComfyUI and Google Colab workflows. Some note it can be computationally intensive (8-10 minutes on high-end GPUs like RTX 5090) and compare it to faster alternatives such as SAM3 for similar tasks.

It has been praised for advancing editable AI images, with users experimenting on manga panels, product designs, and layered text edits. If you are looking to try it, start with the Hugging Face demo.
